_comment: Documents OUTSIDE tools/ whose negative claims are checkable by inversion.
A planning or inventory document says things like 'X does not exist as a script' and 'Y has
never been packaged'. Those are gaps, and a gap is the one kind of claim that gets FIXED --
which makes the sentence recording it false, silently, by someone else's good work. It happened:
the share-pack plan led its gap list with 'the permission-replay validator does not exist as a
script' for as long as it took somebody to write one.
A negative existence claim is testable the other way round. The gate cannot know whether a gap
is CLOSED; it can know whether the artifact the gap says is missing is now present. That is the
whole check, and it is enough -- a stale 'does not exist' beside a file that exists is exactly
the drift a reader cannot detect without going and looking.
WHY THESE FILES ARE NOT UNDER THE MAIN GATE. PLAN-external-share-pack.md carries 25 hits
against the redaction patterns, and needs every one of them: section 3's job is enumerating the
identifier classes to strip, and section 2f names the assets that must never ship. A document
whose subject is the identifiers cannot be scanned for identifiers. It is scanned for the one
thing that IS checkable about it instead.
Citation resolution is deliberately NOT applied here either -- a plan legitimately cites host
configuration and other repositories, and demanding they resolve would produce noise rather
negative_claim_markers: is a plan, not a build
